- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment shows strong downward momentum (change < -0.5) and price is rising, model overestimates; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in high-news-volume periods (≥ 3.0) with mixed sentiment; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for volatility.
- If sentiment change is positive but price is declining, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid “overbought” misalignment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and price is above 10-day average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is bullish but price is flat or declining, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “bullish trap” overreaction.
